subject: DPA clarifications & follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Laura James <laura.james@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & DPA items from our discovery call

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and a couple of follow-ups on the data/privacy items you raised: 

- Scope of data: You mentioned Aurora will send customer support transcripts and partial PII for enrichment. Can you confirm whether the PII fields include full SSNs or only last4? That will drive allowed processing and recommended retention settings.
- Data residency: You prefer US-only storage for logs and payloads. We can pin the control plane and long-term logs to the us-west region; does that meet your compliance needs?
- Retention & logging: Our default session logs (request/response metadata) are retained 30 days for hosted plans; we offer custom retention on Dedicated/Private. If you need shorter retention for full payloads we can propose a config.
- Subprocessors: We use a small set of subprocessors (CDN, monitoring, S3). I attached our current SOC2 summary and the redlined DPA you sent back.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm the PII fields and residency requirement.
2) If possible, have your legal mark up the specific DPA sections you want clarified (controller/processor definitions, breach notice SLA).
3) We’ll schedule a short call with our security lead (Neha) to walk through technical controls — Open slots Monday/Tuesday next week?

Attaching: AuroraTech_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (your redlines), Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform for LLMs
From: Laura James <laura.james@aurora-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Derek Mills <derek.mills@aurora-tech.com>, Aurora Tech Legal <legal@aurora-tech.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & DPA items from our discovery call

Thanks Marissa — that recap is great. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII: We will only be sending names, email addresses, and customer support notes. No SSNs or full payment details. We may include "last4" for verification.
- Residency: US-only for storage of payloads and logs is required. Our compliance team prefers primary storage in us-west and backups in us-central.
- Retention: We cannot retain full payloads longer than 7 days; metadata/telemetry can be kept for 90 days for analytics.
- Controller/Processor: Aurora will be the controller for the customer data and Redwood the processor. We want to ensure the DPA language reflects that and includes an explicit list of subprocessors and the process for prior notice.

Derek from our security team will lead the DPA redlines — copying him. We’re fine to have Neha join a technical call next week. Monday 10–11am PT works.

Laura James
Head of Product, Aurora Tech
laura.james@aurora-tech.com

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & DPA items from our discovery call

Hi Laura/Derek —

Thanks for the details. A few technical notes ahead of Monday’s call: 

- Residency: We can enforce US-only physical storage for S3 buckets and logs. Backup replication to us-central is possible but we can limit backups to encrypted snapshots that are also US-only.
- Retention: For hosted customers we support short payload retention windows via configuration. For Aurora’s requirement (7 days full payloads, 90 days telemetry) we recommend: payload TTL=7d, telemetry TTL=90d. We’ll include TTL config in the DPA appendix.
- Logging controls: We redact PII from logs by default when flagged; however, transcript payloads are stored encrypted at rest and in transit. Access to raw transcripts is limited via RBAC and audited.
- Subprocessors & breach notice: Our DPA lists current subprocessors and requires 30 days notice for material changes; breach notification SLA is 72 hours initial notice + follow-up remediation timeline. If Aurora needs a shorter SLA we can discuss with legal.

I’ll prepare a short technical appendix and join the call Monday 10am PT. Marissa — happy to take action items after the call to update the DPA template.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Derek Mills <derek.mills@aurora-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura James <laura.james@aurora-tech.com>, Aurora Tech Legal <legal@aurora-tech.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & DPA items from our discovery call

Thanks everyone — call was helpful. Quick notes from legal/security: 

- Controller/Processor: We will mark Aurora as controller and Redwood as processor in the DPA. Please ensure the DPA includes: data categories, processing purposes, and a subprocessors exhibit with vendor names + locations.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable. Please provide current subprocessors list and their country of operation.
- Breach notice: 72h initial notification is acceptable; we ask for fuller incident report within 14 days.
- Retention: Confirmed — payload TTL=7d, telemetry=90d. Please include an operational runbook for data deletion on termination.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Share updated DPA with controller/processor language and subprocessors exhibit (Marissa) — attach marked-up DPA and soc2 summary.
2) Share technical appendix and runbook for deletion (Neha).
3) Confirm DocuSign link for signature and provide HubSpot deal record.

Looking forward to the redline.

Derek Mills
Security Operations, Aurora Tech
